themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in East Flatbush spiked to 36 reports THIS WEEK, a 231% increase from the 10.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting sudden infrastructure degradation affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: 36 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.06)
231% spike indicates sudden deterioration rather than chronic issue
Timing coincides with recent weather or construction activity worth investigating
reporting_angles: Interview residents on specific blocks reporting complaints; photograph street conditions
Contact NYC DOT to determine if there's active construction, weather damage, or deferred maintenance affecting the district

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures Exploding
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints in East Flatbush surged to 4 reports last week, a 3100% spike from the 0.1 weekly average, with a z-score of 11.72—the most statistically extreme anomaly in the dataset and a potential sign of grid stress or systemic building code violations.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72)
Highest statistical severity among all identified spikes
Potential indicators: aging building stock, overloaded circuits, deferred maintenance, or infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: FDNY/DOB data: are there electrical fires, outages, or code violations filed in the district this week?
Interview residents about flickering lights, blackouts, or landlord complaints about electrical service

themes_detail.label: Tree and Vegetation Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 1-2 weeks, tree-related complaints have accelerated sharply: dead/dying trees jumped 700% (3 vs. 0.4 weekly average) and overgrown branches surged 367% (7 vs. 1.5 average), suggesting widespread tree decline or storm damage in the district.
evidence: Dead/dying trees: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
Overgrown branches: 7 complaints last week vs. 1.5 baseline (367% increase, z-score: 4.92)
Combined signal suggests rapid vegetation decline across multiple blocks
reporting_angles: NYC Parks Department: are trees being assessed for disease, insect infestation, or drought stress in East Flatbush?
Document specific locations with dead/dying trees; interview residents about safety concerns and visibility obstruction

themes_detail.label: Garbage Disposal System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints in East Flatbush nearly tripled last week, jumping 154% to 7 reports from a 2.8 weekly average, indicating widespread problems with trash removal or building compactors that may signal a sanitation service gap.
evidence: 7 disposal complaints last week vs. 2.8 weekly baseline (154% increase, z-score: 5.13)
Sustained complaints suggest service failure across multiple buildings rather than isolated incidents
Context: East Flatbush has 4,817 heat/hot water complaints (90-day total)—building infrastructure stress may be systemic
reporting_angles: Interview building superintendents and residents about compactor outages or delayed trash pickup
Contact DSNY to check if there are service route issues or equipment problems in the district

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Gaps
themes_detail.summary: Missing street signs jumped 380% to 3 complaints 2 weeks ago from a 0.6 weekly average, suggesting either deliberate vandalism or deferred maintenance creating navigation and safety hazards across the district.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 baseline (380% increase, z-score: 4.91)
Potential indicators: vandalism, wind damage, deferred DOT maintenance
Secondary public safety risk: affects emergency response, wayfinding for elderly/immigrant populations
reporting_angles: Map locations of missing signs; photograph to identify pattern (vandalism vs. deterioration)
NYC DOT: what is the timeline for sign replacement in East Flatbush?
